data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental weather April 2036 Easter trip? You’re in for a treat. Easter weekend (30 March – 6 April) brings mild air, 17-18°C seas and up to 12 hours of sunshine – perfect for cruising the Costa del Sol. This guide gives you the concrete numbers: temperatures, wind, and the best boats in our Puerto Banús fleet for the holiday.

April 2036 Weather Snapshot for Marbella

April is a shoulder month: warm enough for shorts by midday, but with cooler mornings and evenings. Expect air highs of 22°C and lows of 15°C. Sea temperature averages 17-18°C – swimable for the brave, but a wetsuit helps. UV index reaches 6, so sun protection is essential even on cloudy days.

  • Air temperature: 15-22°C
  • Sea temperature: 17-18°C
  • Sunshine: 12 hours/day
  • Wind: Levante 15-20 kts in afternoons
  • Rain: 3-4 days/month, usually brief

Easter Weekend 2036: What to Expect

Easter Sunday falls on 6 April 2036. The holiday week sees a mix of calm mornings and breezier afternoons. The Levante wind – an easterly that funnels through the Strait – can pick up to 15-20 knots by 15:00, creating a slight chop. Our skippers plan routes to sheltered coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés when needed.

For the flattest seas, depart between 10:00 and 15:00. You’ll get the warmest part of the day and the most stable conditions. If you want a sunset cruise, book a 2-hour slot from 17:00 – the light is spectacular, but bring a jacket.

Best Boats for Easter in Our Fleet

All our charters depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks and VAT. For Easter, these are the standouts:

For larger groups, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) and Ferretti 94 (29m) offer extra space and comfort – pricing on request via WhatsApp.

What’s Included in Every Charter

No hidden extras. Every booking includes a professional skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and a generous drinks package: water, soft drinks, beer, white wine and cava, plus light snacks. Spanish IVA (21%) is already in the price. Just bring your swimwear and a camera.

Where to Go: Easter Cruise Routes

With 12 hours of daylight, you can cover a lot. A classic 4-hour trip heads west to Estepona for lunch, then back via the Marbella coastline. For a shorter 2-hour jaunt, cruise to Cabopino and its dunes, or anchor in the calm waters of Río Verde. The Cala del Faro is a favourite for its clear water and rocky backdrop.

If the Levante is strong, your skipper will suggest an easterly route towards Sotogrande, which is often more sheltered. Always trust the skipper’s judgement – safety comes first.

Booking Tips for Easter 2036

Easter is a peak week in Marbella. Book 2-3 weeks ahead to secure your preferred boat. The Mangusta 80 with its free jet ski is especially popular – reserve early. We require a 20% deposit, with the balance due 48 hours before departure. For boats not listed with fixed prices, message us on WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Remember: April weather can change quickly. Check the forecast the morning of your trip and dress in layers. Our team will keep you updated on any schedule adjustments.

Why Choose Boat Rental Marbella

We’re not a broker – these are our own boats, moored in Puerto Banús and maintained to the highest standard. From the sporty Pershing 46 to the spacious Ferretti 94, you’ll find a vessel for every occasion. Our skippers know the coast intimately and will tailor the day to your group’s wishes.

Check our blog for more seasonal guides, or get in touch for a custom quote. Easter 2036 in Marbella is going to be special – make sure you’re on the water.
